title: Women Who Met Jesus
description: In a world that rarely listened to women, Jesus stopped for them, spoke with them, defended them and trusted them with the greatest news in history. His mother Mary, the woman at the well, the woman who touched his robe, the woman caught in adultery, Martha and Mary, the widow and her two mites, the woman who washed his feet with tears, the widow of Nain, the women at the cross, and Mary Magdalene at the empty tomb. From the King James Bible, with a closing prayer.

beats.say: In his world a woman's testimony was not accepted in court, and a respectable teacher did not speak to a woman in public. Jesus did not seem to notice the rule.
Luke tells us that the twelve were with him, and certain women, Mary called Magdalene, and Joanna, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.
They paid for his ministry, travelled with him, stood at his cross when the men had fled, and were the first to see him risen. Here are some of their stories.
Mary said yes to God as a teenager, and gave birth in a stable. She watched her son grow up in Nazareth, and kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
At Cana she noticed the wine running out before anyone else, and told the servants: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. Her last recorded words to anyone, and her best.
And she stood by the cross. A sword shall pierce through thy own soul also, Simeon had warned her, thirty years earlier. Now it did.

Dying, Jesus saw her, and the disciple whom he loved: Woman, behold thy son! Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home. Even on the cross, he took care of his mother.
Noon in Samaria, the hottest hour. A woman came alone to draw water, at the time no one else would be there. Jesus was sitting on the well. Give me to drink.
How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? Jews and Samaritans did not share a cup. Men and women did not share a conversation.

Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
He told her everything: five husbands, and the man she lived with now. Not to shame her. To show her that he knew it all, and was still offering the water.

The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city: Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ? The outcast became the first evangelist to her town.
For twelve years she had bled, and the law called her unclean. She had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse.
She came in the press behind, and touched his garment. For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. And straightway she felt in her body that she was healed.
Jesus stopped the whole procession: Who touched my clothes? She could have slipped away healed. He would not let her leave unseen.
Fearing and trembling, she fell down before him, and told him all the truth. And he said: Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace. After twelve years, someone called her daughter.
At dawn, in the temple, the scribes and Pharisees dragged a woman before Jesus: This woman was taken in adultery, in the very act. Moses commanded that such should be stoned: but what sayest thou?
It was a trap, and she was the bait. Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not.
So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. And he stooped down again, and wrote.
One by one they went out, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last. The oldest knew their own hearts best.
Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee? No man, Lord. Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more. Mercy first, and then a new life.
In Bethany, Martha received him into her house. And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word.
But Martha was cumbered about much serving: Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.
Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
He said her name twice, gently. He was not against her work. He was for her rest. Is there something you are troubled about tonight that could wait, while you sit with him?
A woman of Canaan, a foreigner, followed Jesus crying: Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil. But he answered her not a word.
The disciples wanted her sent away. Jesus tested her: It is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs.
She would not be turned away: Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table. Even the crumbs of his mercy were enough for her.
Then Jesus answered: O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour. Silence from heaven is not always no. Keep asking.
Jesus sat over against the treasury, and watched the people giving. Many that were rich cast in much, and made sure it was heard.
And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites. The smallest coins there were, together worth almost nothing.

Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had.
Heaven does not count the gift. It counts what it cost you. No one in that crowd noticed her. The only one whose opinion mattered noticed nothing else.
A Pharisee named Simon invited Jesus to dinner. Then a woman of the city, which was a sinner, came in with an alabaster box of ointment.
She stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them.
Simon said within himself: This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is. Jesus told him about two debtors, both forgiven. Which of them will love him most?
Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much. Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace. He knew exactly who she was. That was why he let her stay.
At the gate of a town called Nain, a funeral was coming out. A dead man, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. Without husband or son, she had lost her family and her future.
And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not. No one had asked him for anything.
He came and touched the bier: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
He gave him back to her. Jesus saw the widow before he saw the miracle. He sees the one who is grieving tonight too.
When Jesus was arrested, all the disciples forsook him, and fled. But on Golgotha, many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him.
Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee's children. They could not stop it. They would not leave him alone in it.
Afterward they watched where he was laid, and went home to prepare spices. Sometimes faithfulness looks like simply staying, and showing up again in the morning.
Early, when it was yet dark, Mary Magdalene came to the sepulchre, and found the stone taken away. She stood without at the sepulchre weeping.
A man she supposed to be the gardener asked: Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him.
Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master. One word, her own name, and she knew him.

Go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father. Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord. The first witness of the resurrection was a woman whose word the courts would not accept.

chapters.title: A Prayer to the One Who Sees

beats.say: Let us pray. Lord Jesus, you stopped for the woman in the crowd, and sat at the well with the woman nobody spoke to. Stop for me tonight.
Where I am ashamed, say to me what you said to her: Neither do I condemn thee. Where I am bleeding inside, let me touch the hem of your garment and be whole.
When I am troubled about many things, sit me down at your feet. Accept my two mites, the small things I have to give. And for the grieving tonight, say: Weep not.
Call me by name, as you called Mary in the garden, and send me to tell someone I have seen the Lord. Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace. Amen.
